etymology: Reduplication of 紧 (tight, taut). 紧 itself originally depicted strings under tension.

examples.pinyin: Tā jǐn jǐn zhuā zhù wǒ de shǒu.
examples.english: He held my hand tightly.

examples.pinyin: Zhè liǎng gè wèn tí jǐn jǐn xiāng lián.
examples.english: These two issues are closely linked.

usage_notes: Emphasizes the degree of tightness or closeness.

mnemonic: The color you get when this (此) silk thread (纟) is dyed.
etymology: From 糸/纟 (silk, thread) + 此 (this, phonetic). Related to the color of silk.

examples.pinyin: Tā zuì xǐ huān zǐ sè de qún zi.
examples.english: She likes purple dresses the most.

examples.pinyin: Bàng wǎn de tiān kōng shì zǐ sè de.
examples.english: The evening sky is purple.

usage_notes: Used as 紫色的 or in color compounds like 紫罗兰 (violet).

mnemonic: Numerous/complex (繁) and glorious/flourishing (荣).
etymology: 繁 (numerous, complicated) + 榮 (glory, flourish). 榮 originally depicted trees in bloom.

examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò chéng shì fēi cháng fán róng.
examples.english: This city is very prosperous.

examples.chinese: 我们祝贵公司繁荣昌盛。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ men zhù guì gōng sī fán róng chāng shèng.
examples.english: We wish your company prosperity and success.

usage_notes: Often describes economies, markets, or eras.

mnemonic: An agreement (约) that binds/ties up (束).
etymology: 約 (agreement, bind) + 束 (to bind, tie up).

examples.chinese: 我们要学会约束自己的行为。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ men yào xué huì yuē shù zì jǐ de xíng wéi.
examples.english: We must learn to restrain our own behavior.

examples.chinese: 这个项目有很多时间约束。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge xiàng mù yǒu hěn duō shí jiān yuē shù.
examples.english: This project has a lot of time constraints.

usage_notes: Can be external rules or self-discipline.

mnemonic: A thread (线) you search for/sniff out (索).
etymology: 線/线 (thread, line) + 索 (large rope, to search). A metaphorical thread to follow.

examples.chinese: 警察找到了一些破案的线索。
examples.pinyin: Jǐng chá zhǎo dào le yī xiē pò àn de xiàn suǒ.
examples.english: The police found some clues to solve the case.

examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo xiàn suǒ hěn zhòng yào.
examples.english: This clue is very important.

usage_notes: Used in detective work, mysteries, or figuring out problems.

mnemonic: Weaving (织) threads together into a structured group (组).
etymology: 組 (group, form) + 織 (to weave). Metaphor for bringing elements together into a structure.

examples.chinese: 他在一个非营利组织工作。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài yī gè fēi yíng lì zǔ zhī gōng zuò.
examples.english: He works for a non-profit organization.

examples.chinese: 周末我们组织了一次郊游。
examples.pinyin: Zhōu mò wǒ men zǔ zhī le yī cì jiāo yóu.
examples.english: We organized a picnic over the weekend.

usage_notes: Very common word for any type of organized group (company, club, body tissue).

mnemonic: 自己愿意 = 'myself + willing'
etymology: 自 (self) + 愿 (wish, desire)

examples.chinese: 我是自愿参加这个活动的。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ shì zì yuàn cān jiā zhè ge huó dòng de.
examples.english: I participated in this activity voluntarily.

examples.pinyin: Zhè shì zì yuàn bào míng, bù miǎn qiǎng.
examples.english: This is voluntary sign-up, no pressure.

usage_notes: Can be used like an adjective (自愿的行为) or a verb (我自愿去).

mnemonic: 自己杀自己。
etymology: 自 (self) + 杀 (kill)

examples.pinyin: Qǐng bù yào yǒu zì shā de niàn tou.
examples.english: Please don't have thoughts of suicide.

examples.chinese: 遇到困难可以求助，别想不开。
examples.pinyin: Yù dào kùn nán kě yǐ qiú zhù, bié xiǎng bu kāi.
examples.english: You can ask for help when in trouble, don't despair.

usage_notes: Sensitive topic. 想不开 is a more casual way to talk about despair.

mnemonic: 自己感到豪气 (self + heroic spirit).
etymology: 自 (self) + 豪 (heroic, grand)

examples.chinese: 他为儿子的成绩感到自豪。
examples.pinyin: Tā wèi ér zi de chéng jì gǎn dào zì háo.
examples.english: He is proud of his son's achievements.

examples.chinese: 看到国家的进步，我很自豪。
examples.pinyin: Kàn dào guó jiā de jìn bù, wǒ hěn zì háo.
examples.english: Seeing the country's progress makes me very proud.

usage_notes: Often used with 感到 or 觉得. More positive than 骄傲, which can also mean 'arrogant'.

mnemonic: 自大加一点就臭了 (The character looks like 自 + a dot).
etymology: Pictograph of a dog sniffing; originally related to smell.

examples.chinese: 厕所好臭，快去处理一下。
examples.pinyin: Cè suǒ hǎo chòu, kuài qù chǔ lǐ yī xià.
examples.english: The toilet is so smelly, go deal with it quickly.

examples.pinyin: Zhè shuāng wà zi tài chòu le!
examples.english: These socks are too stinky!

usage_notes: Can also be used metaphorically for 'disgraceful' (e.g., 臭名远扬).

mnemonic: 一只鸟落到地上 (Looks like a bird landing on ground).
etymology: Pictograph of an arrow hitting a target, indicating arrival or reaching.

examples.chinese: 营业时间从早上九点至晚上六点。
examples.pinyin: Yíng yè shí jiān cóng zǎo shang jiǔ diǎn zhì wǎn shang liù diǎn.
examples.english: Business hours are from 9 AM to 6 PM.

examples.pinyin: Tā gāo xìng zhì jí.
examples.english: He is extremely happy.

usage_notes: More formal/written than 到. Common in compounds (至今, 至少).

english: to be reluctant to part with/give up
mnemonic: 舍不得花钱 = can't bear to spend money.
etymology: 舍 (give up, abandon) + 不 (not) + 得 (can) → 'cannot give up'.

examples.chinese: 我舍不得扔掉这些旧玩具。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ shě bu de rēng diào zhè xiē jiù wán jù.
examples.english: I can't bear to throw away these old toys.

examples.chinese: 他太抠了，连杯奶茶都舍不得买。
examples.pinyin: Tā tài kōu le, lián bēi nǎi chá dōu shě bu de mǎi.
examples.english: He's too stingy, he can't even bring himself to buy a cup of milk tea.

usage_notes: A common and very useful colloquial phrase. Followed by a verb or noun.

english: to be willing to part with/give up
mnemonic: 舍得花钱 = willing to spend money.
etymology: 舍 (give up) + 得 (can) → 'can give up'.

examples.chinese: 为了孩子，他什么都舍得。
examples.pinyin: Wèi le hái zi, tā shén me dōu shě de.
examples.english: For his child, he's willing to give up anything.

examples.chinese: 你舍得花这么多钱买包吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ shě de huā zhè me duō qián mǎi bāo ma?
examples.english: Are you willing to spend this much money on a bag?

usage_notes: The positive counterpart of 舍不得. Often used in questions or conditional statements.

mnemonic: 一个人在跳舞 (The character looks like a dancing figure).
etymology: Pictograph of a person dancing with sleeves flowing.

examples.chinese: 周末我们去舞厅跳舞吧！
examples.pinyin: Zhōu mò wǒ men qù wǔ tīng tiào wǔ ba!
examples.english: Let's go dancing at the dance hall this weekend!

examples.pinyin: Tā wǔ tiào de zhēn hǎo.
examples.english: She dances really well.

usage_notes: As a verb, usually combined with 跳 (跳舞).

mnemonic: 又艰难又辛苦。
etymology: 艰 (difficult) + 苦 (bitter, hardship)

examples.pinyin: Chuàng yè de guò chéng fēi cháng jiān kǔ.
examples.english: The process of starting a business is very arduous.

examples.pinyin: Tā men guò zhe jiān kǔ de shēng huó.
examples.english: They live a hard life.

usage_notes: Emphasizes enduring physical/material hardships. Often describes conditions,生活, 奋斗.

mnemonic: 又艰又难，双倍困难。
etymology: 艰 (difficult) + 难 (difficult)

examples.pinyin: Zuò chū zhè ge jué dìng hěn jiān nán.
examples.english: Making this decision was very difficult.

examples.pinyin: Gōng sī mù qián chǔ jìng jiān nán.
examples.english: The company is in a difficult situation now.

usage_notes: Broader than 艰苦, can describe abstract difficulties like decisions, situations, times.

mnemonic: 长满草的原野。
etymology: 草 (grass) + 原 (plain, field)

examples.chinese: 我想去内蒙古的大草原看看。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng qù Nèi Měng Gǔ de dà cǎo yuán kàn kan.
examples.english: I want to go see the vast grasslands of Inner Mongolia.

examples.pinyin: Cǎo yuán shang de fēng jǐng zhēn měi.
examples.english: The scenery on the grassland is really beautiful.

mnemonic: 让计划落到实地。
etymology: 落 (fall, land) + 实 (solid, real) → 'to land solidly'.

examples.chinese: 这个计划下周必须落实。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge jì huà xià zhōu bì xū luò shí.
examples.english: This plan must be implemented next week.

examples.chinese: 老板，您说的那件事落实了吗？
examples.pinyin: Lǎo bǎn, nín shuō de nà jiàn shì luò shí le ma?
examples.english: Boss, has that thing you mentioned been carried out?

usage_notes: Common in work/business contexts. Often takes objects like 计划, 政策, 任务.

mnemonic: 草字头下的水果。
etymology: A transliteration of an ancient Iranian word for grape, borrowed along the Silk Road.

examples.pinyin: Gěi wǒ xǐ yī chuàn pú tao chī.
examples.english: Wash a bunch of grapes for me to eat.

examples.pinyin: Zhè pú tao yǒu diǎn suān.
examples.english: These grapes are a bit sour.

usage_notes: Pinyin is written as two separate words (pú tao) but it's one noun. 提子 is another word for grape (often seedless).

mnemonic: 葡萄做的酒。
etymology: 葡萄 (grape) + 酒 (alcohol)

examples.pinyin: Wǎn cān hē diǎn hóng pú tao jiǔ ma?
examples.english: Shall we have some red wine with dinner?

examples.chinese: 这瓶葡萄酒是朋友送的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè píng pú tao jiǔ shì péng you sòng de.
examples.english: This bottle of wine was a gift from a friend.

usage_notes: Often specified as 红葡萄酒 (red wine) or 白葡萄酒 (white wine). 红酒 usually means red wine specifically.

mnemonic: 又薄又弱。
etymology: 薄 (thin, weak) + 弱 (weak)

examples.chinese: 我的数学基础比较薄弱。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de shù xué jī chǔ bǐ jiào bó ruò.
examples.english: My foundation in math is relatively weak.

examples.chinese: 这是公司管理最薄弱的环节。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì gōng sī guǎn lǐ zuì bó ruò de huán jié.
examples.english: This is the weakest link in the company's management.

usage_notes: Usually describes abstract things like 基础, 环节, 环节, 意志, not physical strength.

mnemonic: 老虎额头上的'王'字。
etymology: Pictograph of a striped tiger.

examples.pinyin: Dòng wù yuán li yǒu zhī dà lǎo hǔ.
examples.english: There's a big tiger in the zoo.

examples.pinyin: Tā shēng qì qǐ lái xiàng zhī lǎo hǔ.
examples.english: When he gets angry, he's like a tiger.

usage_notes: Usually 老虎 in spoken Chinese. 虎 is more common in writing, names, and idioms (虎年).

mnemonic: 心里空空的，才能装下新东西。
etymology: 虚 (empty, humble) + 心 (heart, mind)

examples.chinese: 你要虚心接受别人的意见。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yào xū xīn jiē shòu bié rén de yì jiàn.
examples.english: You should be open-minded and accept others' opinions.

examples.pinyin: Tā xué xí hěn xū xīn.
examples.english: He is very modest in his studies.

usage_notes: Specifically about being receptive to learning or criticism. Often used with 学习, 接受, 请教.

mnemonic: 一条弯曲爬行的虫。
etymology: Pictograph of a snake with a large head and long body.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ chāo pà shé!
examples.english: I'm super afraid of snakes!

examples.pinyin: Cǎo cóng li hǎo xiàng yǒu tiáo shé.
examples.english: There seems to be a snake in the grass.

mnemonic: 鸡蛋做的糕。
etymology: 蛋 (egg) + 糕 (cake, pastry) → western-style cake.

examples.pinyin: Shēng rì kuài lè! Kuài lái qiē dàn gāo!
examples.english: Happy birthday! Come cut the cake!

examples.chinese: 这家店的蛋糕特别好吃。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn de dàn gāo tè bié hǎo chī.
examples.english: The cakes from this shop are especially delicious.

usage_notes: Refers to western-style cakes. Chinese-style steamed cakes are often 糕点 or specific names.

mnemonic: 虫字旁，胡和蝶的合体。
etymology: Originally 胡蝶, where 胡 might refer to 'whiskers' (antennae) and 蝶 is the core character for butterfly.

examples.pinyin: Kàn, yǒu zhī hú dié!
examples.english: Look, there's a butterfly!

examples.pinyin: Huā yuán li hú dié fēi lái fēi qù.
examples.english: Butterflies are flying around in the garden.

mnemonic: 车在行进。
etymology: 行 (to go, to travel) + 驶 (to drive, to speed)

examples.chinese: 高速公路上行驶请注意安全。
examples.pinyin: Gāo sù gōng lù shang xíng shǐ qǐng zhù yì ān quán.
examples.english: Please drive safely on the highway.

examples.chinese: 这辆车行驶了十万公里。
examples.pinyin: Zhè liàng chē xíng shǐ le shí wàn gōng lǐ.
examples.english: This car has traveled 100,000 kilometers.

usage_notes: More formal than 开车. Subject is usually the vehicle, not the driver. 驾驶 is more about the act of driving.

mnemonic: 补上损失，让人尝到公平。
etymology: 补 (mend, compensate) + 偿 (repay, compensate)

examples.pinyin: Gōng sī huì bǔ cháng nǐ de sǔn shī.
examples.english: The company will compensate you for your loss.

examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎng yào yī diǎn jīng shén bǔ cháng.
examples.english: He wants some compensation for emotional distress.

usage_notes: Can be for material or non-material losses (精神补偿). Often used in formal or legal contexts.

mnemonic: 贴补家用。
etymology: 补 (supplement) + 贴 (paste, subsidize) → 'to subsidize'.

examples.chinese: 公司有交通补贴和餐补。
examples.pinyin: Gōng sī yǒu jiāo tōng bǔ tiē hé cān bǔ.
examples.english: The company provides transportation and meal subsidies.

examples.pinyin: Zhèng fǔ bǔ tiē le nóng mín.
examples.english: The government subsidized the farmers.

usage_notes: Common workplace word for benefits. Also used for government support.

mnemonic: 被人推动，而不是自己主动。
etymology: 被 (by [passive marker]) + 动 (move) → 'moved by others'.

examples.pinyin: Tā zǒng shì chǔ yú bèi dòng zhuàng tài.
examples.english: He is always in a passive state.

examples.chinese: 别那么被动，要主动一点！
examples.pinyin: Bié nà me bèi dòng, yào zhǔ dòng yī diǎn!
examples.english: Don't be so passive, be more proactive!

usage_notes: Opposite of 主动. Often has a negative connotation of lacking initiative.

mnemonic: 装点修饰。
etymology: 装 (to dress up, to install) + 饰 (to adorn, ornament)

examples.chinese: 我们买了彩灯装饰圣诞树。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ men mǎi le cǎi dēng zhuāng shì shèng dàn shù.
examples.english: We bought string lights to decorate the Christmas tree.

examples.chinese: 这个房间的装饰很现代。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge fáng jiān de zhuāng shì hěn xiàn dài.
examples.english: The decoration of this room is very modern.

usage_notes: Can refer to the act of decorating or the decorative items themselves.

mnemonic: A red fruit from the west: 西 (west) + 红 (red) + 柿 (persimmon).
etymology: Literally 'western red persimmon'. 西 (west) indicates it was introduced from the West, 红 (red) describes its color, 柿 (persimmon) likens it to that fruit.

measure_word.example: 一个西红柿 (yī gè xī hóng shì)

examples.chinese: 晚饭做西红柿炒鸡蛋吧。
examples.pinyin: Wǎn fàn zuò xī hóng shì chǎo jī dàn ba.
examples.english: Let's cook scrambled eggs with tomatoes for dinner.

examples.pinyin: Zhè gè xī hóng shì hǎo suān.
examples.english: This tomato is so sour.

mnemonic: Western clothes: 西 (west) + 装 (clothing/attire).
etymology: Compound of 西 (west) + 装 (clothing), indicating clothing introduced from the West.

measure_word.example: 一套西装 (yī tào xī zhuāng)

examples.pinyin: Míng tiān miàn shì yào chuān xī zhuāng.
examples.english: You need to wear a suit for tomorrow's interview.

examples.pinyin: Zhè tào xī zhuāng tài guì le.
examples.english: This suit is too expensive.

usage_notes: Often refers specifically to a Western-style suit jacket and trousers.

mnemonic: Planning a path with a compass: 规 (compass/rules) + 划 (to plan).
etymology: 规 originally meant a compass for drawing circles, implying rules or standards. 划 means to delineate or plan. Together they mean making a plan according to certain standards.

examples.chinese: 好好规划一下你的假期。
examples.pinyin: Hǎo hǎo guī huà yī xià nǐ de jià qī.
examples.english: Plan your holiday properly.

examples.chinese: 这是我们公司的五年规划。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒ men gōng sī de wǔ nián guī huà.
examples.english: This is our company's five-year plan.

usage_notes: More formal and strategic than 计划 (jì huà). Often used for long-term or large-scale planning.

mnemonic: Look at it and become that: 视 (to look at/regard) + 为 (to act as/be).
etymology: 视 means to look at or regard. 为 means to act as or to be. Combined, it means 'to regard (something) as (something else)'.

examples.chinese: 我一直把你视为最好的朋友。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yī zhí bǎ nǐ shì wéi zuì hǎo de péng you.
examples.english: I have always regarded you as my best friend.

examples.chinese: 这个错误被视为很严重。
examples.pinyin: Zhè gè cuò wù bèi shì wéi hěn yán zhòng.
examples.english: This mistake is regarded as very serious.

usage_notes: Used in the pattern "把 A 视为 B" or "被 视为". More formal than 当成 (dàng chéng).

mnemonic: See the frequency: 视 (vision/see) + 频 (frequency). It's the visual frequency signal.
etymology: 视 (vision, to see) + 频 (frequency, wave). A modern compound for the visual frequency signals that make up moving images.

measure_word.example: 一段视频 (yī duàn shì pín)

examples.chinese: 我在网上看到一个有趣的视频。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zài wǎng shàng kàn dào yī gè yǒu qù de shì pín.
examples.english: I saw an interesting video online.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ men shì pín liáo tiān ba.
examples.english: Let's have a video chat.

usage_notes: Very common word for any digital video content.

mnemonic: Untie and release: 解 (to untie) + 放 (to release).
etymology: 解 means to untie or loosen. 放 means to release or let go. Combined, it means to set free from bondage or constraints.

examples.chinese: 新技术解放了我们的双手。
examples.pinyin: Xīn jì shù jiě fàng le wǒ men de shuāng shǒu.
examples.english: New technology has freed our hands.

examples.chinese: 他觉得自己从责任中解放出来了。
examples.pinyin: Tā jué de zì jǐ cóng zé rèn zhōng jiě fàng chū lái le.
examples.english: He felt liberated from his responsibilities.

usage_notes: Can be used for physical, mental, or social liberation. It has significant historical connotations in modern Chinese context.

mnemonic: Person who explains and narrates: 解 (explain) + 说 (speak) + 员 (person).
etymology: 解 (to explain) + 说 (to speak) + 员 (person engaged in an activity). A person who provides spoken explanations.

measure_word.example: 一位解说员 (yī wèi jiě shuō yuán)

examples.chinese: 这个体育解说员的声音很有激情。
examples.pinyin: Zhè gè tǐ yù jiě shuō yuán de shēng yīn hěn yǒu jī qíng.
examples.english: This sports commentator's voice is very passionate.

examples.chinese: 博物馆有解说员带你参观。
examples.pinyin: Bó wù guǎn yǒu jiě shuō yuán dài nǐ cān guān.
examples.english: The museum has a guide to show you around.

usage_notes: Common for sports, events, museum tours, etc.

mnemonic: Untie and get rid of: 解 (untie) + 除 (remove).
etymology: 解 (to untie, loosen) + 除 (to remove, eliminate). To untie and take away a constraint or condition.

examples.chinese: 软件终于解除了对这个网站的屏蔽。
examples.pinyin: Ruǎn jiàn zhōng yú jiě chú le duì zhè gè wǎng zhàn de píng bì.
examples.english: The software finally lifted the block on this website.

examples.pinyin: Gōng sī jiě chú le tā de zhí wù.
examples.english: The company removed him from his position.

usage_notes: Often used for formal removal of contracts, bans, positions, or states (like warnings).

mnemonic: Words and language: 言 (speech) + 语 (language).
etymology: A compound of near-synonyms. 言 means to speak or words. 语 means language or speech.

examples.chinese: 他的言语之间充满了自信。
examples.pinyin: Tā de yán yǔ zhī jiān chōng mǎn le zì xìn.
examples.english: His speech is full of confidence.

examples.pinyin: Bié tài zài yì bié rén de yán yǔ.
examples.english: Don't pay too much attention to other people's words.

usage_notes: More formal/literary than 话 (huà). Often used for the content or quality of what is said.

mnemonic: Alert and tell: 警 (alert/police) + 告 (to tell).
etymology: 警 means to alert or warn (also police). 告 means to tell or inform. Combined, it means to give an alert or caution.

measure_word.example: 一个警告 (yī gè jǐng gào)

examples.chinese: 医生警告他不要再抽烟了。
examples.pinyin: Yī shēng jǐng gào tā bú yào zài chōu yān le.
examples.english: The doctor warned him not to smoke anymore.

examples.chinese: 我收到了系统的黄色警告。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ shōu dào le xì tǒng de huáng sè jǐng gào.
examples.english: I received a yellow warning from the system.

mnemonic: Use words (讠) to acknowledge someone's blade (刀).
etymology: Simplified from 認. Composed of 讠(speech) and 忍 (endure, but here phonetic). The core meaning involves acknowledging with words.

examples.chinese: 你认得出这是谁的字吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ rèn de chū zhè shì shuí de zì ma?
examples.english: Can you recognize whose handwriting this is?

examples.pinyin: Wǒ rèn le, zhè cì shì wǒ cuò le.
examples.english: I admit it, I was wrong this time.

usage_notes: A versatile verb often used in compounds (认识, 认为). By itself, it can mean 'to recognize' or 'to admit/accept' (a fact).

mnemonic: Recognize and set it: 认 (recognize) + 定 (to set/fix).
etymology: 认 (to recognize/admit) + 定 (to fix/set). To recognize something and fix it as true or certain.

examples.chinese: 我认定他就是我要找的人。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ rèn dìng tā jiù shì wǒ yào zhǎo de rén.
examples.english: I firmly believe he is the person I'm looking for.

examples.chinese: 警方认定这是一起意外。
examples.pinyin: Jǐng fāng rèn dìng zhè shì yī qǐ yì wài.
examples.english: The police determined it was an accident.

usage_notes: Stronger and more conclusive than 认为 (rèn wéi).

mnemonic: Discuss and get disgusted: 讨 (discuss/beg) + 厌 (disgust).
etymology: 讨 originally meant to discuss or demand, later引申 to provoke. 厌 means to detest or be disgusted. Combined, it means something that provokes disgust.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ tǎo yàn xià yǔ tiān.
examples.english: I dislike rainy days.

examples.pinyin: Zhè gè rén zhēn tǎo yàn!
examples.english: This person is so annoying!

usage_notes: Common for expressing dislike or describing something annoying. Less strong than 恨 (hèn - to hate).

mnemonic: Record and recall: 记 (record) + 忆 (recall).
etymology: 记 means to record or remember. 忆 means to recall or recollect. Together they encompass the act of memorizing and recalling.

examples.chinese: 我对这件事没有一点记忆。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ duì zhè jiàn shì méi yǒu yī diǎn jì yì.
examples.english: I have no memory of this event at all.

examples.chinese: 这个味道让我记忆深刻。
examples.pinyin: Zhè gè wèi dào ràng wǒ jì yì shēn kè.
examples.english: This smell left a deep impression on me.

usage_notes: The noun is more common. As a verb, it's more literary; 记住 (jì zhù) is more casual for 'to remember'.

mnemonic: Allow and approve: 许 (allow) + 可 (can/approve).
etymology: 许 means to allow or promise. 可 means can or may. Combined, it means to give allowance or approval.

examples.pinyin: Méi yǒu xǔ kě bù néng jìn rù.
examples.english: No entry without permission.

examples.chinese: 老板许可了我们的计划。
examples.pinyin: Lǎo bǎn xǔ kě le wǒ men de jì huà.
examples.english: The boss permitted our plan.

usage_notes: More formal than 让 (ràng) or 可以 (kě yǐ). Often used for official, written, or parental permission.

mnemonic: Set up a thought: 设 (set up) + 想 (think).
etymology: 设 means to set up or establish. 想 means to think. To set up a thought in your mind.

examples.chinese: 你设想过十年后的生活吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ shè xiǎng guò shí nián hòu de shēng huó ma?
examples.english: Have you imagined what life will be like in ten years?

examples.pinyin: Zhè gè shè xiǎng hěn dà dǎn.
examples.english: This conception is very bold.

usage_notes: Can mean a mental plan or scenario, often hypothetical.

mnemonic: Proof document: 证 (proof) + 书 (document/book).
etymology: 证 means to prove or evidence. 书 means document or book. A document that proves something.

measure_word.example: 一张证书 (yī zhāng zhèng shū)

examples.chinese: 我上周拿到了驾照证书。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ shàng zhōu ná dào le jià zhào zhèng shū.
examples.english: I got my driver's license certificate last week.

examples.chinese: 这个证书在网上能查到吗？
examples.pinyin: Zhè gè zhèng shū zài wǎng shàng néng chá dào ma?
examples.english: Can this certificate be verified online?

usage_notes: For diplomas, licenses, awards, etc.

mnemonic: Prove it's real: 证 (prove) + 实 (real/true).
etymology: 证 (to prove, evidence) + 实 (real, solid, true). To prove something is true or real.

examples.chinese: 这条新闻已经被证实了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo xīn wén yǐ jīng bèi zhèng shí le.
examples.english: This piece of news has already been confirmed.

examples.chinese: 实验结果证实了我的猜想。
examples.pinyin: Shí yàn jié guǒ zhèng shí le wǒ de cāi xiǎng.
examples.english: The experiment results confirmed my guess.

usage_notes: Focuses on verifying the truth of information, rumors, theories, etc.

mnemonic: Weigh and estimate: 评 (judge/comment) + 估 (estimate).
etymology: 评 (to judge, comment, review) + 估 (to estimate, appraise). To judge and estimate value or quality.

examples.chinese: 公司每年都会评估员工的表现。
examples.pinyin: Gōng sī měi nián dōu huì píng gū yuán gōng de biǎo xiàn.
examples.english: The company evaluates employees' performance every year.

examples.chinese: 我们需要做个风险评估。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ men xū yào zuò gè fēng xiǎn píng gū.
examples.english: We need to do a risk assessment.

usage_notes: Often used in professional, academic, or formal contexts.

mnemonic: Judge and discuss: 评 (judge) + 论 (discuss).
etymology: 评 (to judge, comment) + 论 (to discuss, theory). To discuss and judge something.

measure_word.example: 一条评论 (yī tiáo píng lùn)

examples.pinyin: Bié zài xià miàn luàn píng lùn.
examples.english: Don't leave random comments below.

examples.pinyin: Zhè bù diàn yǐng de píng lùn hěn hǎo.
examples.english: The reviews for this movie are very good.

usage_notes: Common for online comments, reviews, or critiques.

mnemonic: Examine and decide: 诊 (examine) + 断 (judge/decide).
etymology: 诊 means to examine (a patient). 断 means to judge or decide. To examine and judge an illness.

examples.pinyin: Yī shēng zhěn duàn wǒ dé le liú gǎn.
examples.english: The doctor diagnosed me with the flu.

examples.pinyin: Zhè gè zhěn duàn jié guǒ zhǔn què ma?
examples.english: Is this diagnosis accurate?

usage_notes: Primarily medical, but can be used metaphorically (e.g., diagnosing a computer problem).

mnemonic: Try and picture it: 试 (try) + 图 (plan/picture).
etymology: 试 (to try, test) + 图 (to plan, intend, scheme). To try with an intention or plan.

examples.chinese: 他试图打开那扇锁着的门。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì tú dǎ kāi nà shàn suǒ zhe de mén.
examples.english: He tried to open that locked door.

examples.pinyin: Bié shì tú shuō fú wǒ, méi yòng de.
examples.english: Don't try to persuade me, it's useless.

usage_notes: Often followed by another verb phrase. More formal/literary than 想 (xiǎng) or 打算 (dǎ suàn).

mnemonic: Poem and song: 诗 (poem) + 歌 (song).
etymology: A compound of near-synonyms. 诗 means poem. 歌 means song. Together they refer to the art of lyrical verse.

measure_word.example: 一首诗歌 (yī shǒu shī gē)

examples.pinyin: Tā xǐ huān xiě xiàn dài shī gē.
examples.english: He likes to write modern poetry.

examples.pinyin: Zhè shǒu shī gē hěn yǒu yì jìng.
examples.english: This poem has a very artistic mood.

usage_notes: A general term for poetry as an art form or a specific poem.

mnemonic: Seek and ask: 询 (inquire) + 问 (ask).
etymology: A compound of near-synonyms. 询 means to ask or consult. 问 means to ask. Together they emphasize a formal or careful inquiry.

examples.chinese: 我去前台询问一下价格。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ qù qián tái xún wèn yī xià jià gé.
examples.english: I'll go ask the front desk about the price.

examples.pinyin: Jǐng chá zhèng zài xún wèn mù jī zhě.
examples.english: The police are questioning the eyewitness.

usage_notes: More polite and formal than simply 问 (wèn). Often used for official or detailed inquiries.

mnemonic: Quiet and fine details: 详 (detailed/quiet) + 细 (fine/small).
etymology: 详 means detailed, thorough, or peaceful. 细 means fine, small, or meticulous. Combined, it emphasizes meticulous detail.

examples.chinese: 我需要一份详细的报告。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xū yào yī fèn xiáng xì de bào gào.
examples.english: I need a detailed report.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ néng shuō de xiáng xì yī diǎn ma?
examples.english: Can you explain in more detail?

usage_notes: Often used with 地 (de) as an adverb: 详细地解释 (xiáng xì de jiě shì - explain in detail).

mnemonic: Think of '误(wù)' as 'mistake' and '解(jiě)' as 'explanation/understand'. So it's a mistake in understanding.
etymology: 误: originally meant 'to err' or 'to misspeak'. 解: means to untie, explain, or understand. Together, 'to err in understanding'.

examples.chinese: 你误解我的意思了，我不是那个意思。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ wù jiě wǒ de yì si le, wǒ bú shì nà ge yì si.
examples.english: You misunderstood me, that's not what I meant.

examples.chinese: 这个误解让我们的关系变差了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge wù jiě ràng wǒ men de guān xì biàn chà le.
examples.english: This misunderstanding made our relationship worse.

usage_notes: Can be used as a verb ('你误解了') or a noun ('这是一个误解').

english: way of saying it; version (of a story)
mnemonic: It's literally how you '说(shuō)' (speak) and what '法(fǎ)' (method/way). So the 'way of speaking' about something.
etymology: 说: to speak, to say. 法: method, way, law. Combined, it refers to a particular way of expressing something.

examples.chinese: 对于这件事，他给出了另一个说法。
examples.pinyin: Duì yú zhè jiàn shì, tā gěi chū le lìng yī gè shuō fǎ.
examples.english: Regarding this matter, he gave a different version of the story.

examples.chinese: 这个汉字有好几种说法。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge hàn zì yǒu hǎo jǐ zhǒng shuō fǎ.
examples.english: There are several ways to pronounce this Chinese character.

usage_notes: Often used when comparing different versions or explanations of an event.

mnemonic: Think of a '课(kè)' (lesson/class) and its '题(tí)' (topic/question). It's the big question for your class or project.
etymology: 课: originally meant to test or examine; later extended to mean lesson/subject. 题: topic, subject, question. Together, a subject for study or a problem to be solved.

examples.chinese: 这个课题太难了，我研究了很久。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge kè tí tài nán le, wǒ yán jiū le hěn jiǔ.
examples.english: This research topic is too difficult; I've been studying it for a long time.

examples.chinese: 保护环境是我们社会的重要课题。
examples.pinyin: Bǎo hù huán jìng shì wǒ men shè huì de zhòng yào kè tí.
examples.english: Protecting the environment is an important issue for our society.

usage_notes: More formal than '问题(wèn tí)'. Often used in academic, work, or serious discussion contexts.

english: to transfer; to mobilize; to arouse
mnemonic: Think of a boss '调(diào)' (transferring) someone to make them '动(dòng)' (move).
etymology: 调: to transfer, to blend. 动: to move, to act. Combined, it means to transfer personnel or to mobilize resources/emotions.

examples.chinese: 公司把我调动到上海分公司了。
examples.pinyin: Gōng sī bǎ wǒ diào dòng dào Shàng hǎi fēn gōng sī le.
examples.english: The company transferred me to the Shanghai branch.

examples.chinese: 这个演讲成功调动了大家的积极性。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge yǎn jiǎng chéng gōng diào dòng le dà jiā de jī jí xìng.
examples.english: This speech successfully mobilized everyone's enthusiasm.

usage_notes: Commonly used for job transfers ('调动工作') and for arousing emotions or enthusiasm.

mnemonic: Think of '调(tiáo)' as 'adjust' (like 空调 - air conditioner) and '节(jié)' as 'control/knot'. To adjust and control something.
etymology: 调: to harmonize, to blend, to adjust. 节: joint, festival, to regulate. Together, it means to adjust to a proper state.

examples.chinese: 你能帮我把空调调节一下吗？太热了。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ néng bāng wǒ bǎ kōng tiáo tiáo jié yī xià ma? Tài rè le.
examples.english: Can you help me adjust the air conditioner? It's too hot.

examples.chinese: 你要学会调节自己的情绪。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yào xué huì tiáo jié zì jǐ de qíng xù.
examples.english: You need to learn to regulate your emotions.

usage_notes: Used for adjusting physical things (temperature, volume) and abstract things (mood, relationships).

mnemonic: Think of someone stepping in to '调(tiáo)' (harmonize) and '解(jiě)' (solve) a fight.
etymology: 调: to harmonize. 解: to untie, to solve. Together, it means to harmonize a dispute, to mediate.

examples.chinese: 邻居吵架了，居委会的人来调解。
examples.pinyin: Lín jū chǎo jià le, jū wěi huì de rén lái tiáo jiě.
examples.english: The neighbors were arguing, so the neighborhood committee came to mediate.

examples.chinese: 经过调解，双方都同意各退一步。
examples.pinyin: Jīng guò tiáo jiě, shuāng fāng dōu tóng yì gè tuì yī bù.
examples.english: After mediation, both parties agreed to compromise.

usage_notes: Specifically used for resolving conflicts or disputes between people/groups.

mnemonic: It's exactly what it sounds like: '豆(dòu)' (bean) '制(zhì)' (made) '品(pǐn)' (products).
etymology: 豆: bean. 制: to make, to manufacture. 品: product, article, grade. Together, it means 'bean-made products'.

examples.chinese: 豆腐、豆浆都是常见的豆制品。
examples.pinyin: Dòu fu, dòu jiāng dōu shì cháng jiàn de dòu zhì pǐn.
examples.english: Tofu and soy milk are both common bean products.

examples.chinese: 很多素食者喜欢吃豆制品。
examples.pinyin: Hěn duō sù shí zhě xǐ huān chī dòu zhì pǐn.
examples.english: Many vegetarians like to eat bean products.

usage_notes: A general category term for foods made from soybeans or other beans (tofu, soy milk, tempeh, etc.).

mnemonic: Think of something that makes you '象(xiàng)' (imagine) and '征(zhēng)' (sign/prove) a bigger idea, like a dove symbolizing peace.
etymology: 象: appearance, image, to resemble. 征: sign, proof, to journey. Combined, it refers to something that serves as a sign or emblem of something else.

examples.chinese: 熊猫是中国的象征之一。
examples.pinyin: Xióng māo shì Zhōng guó de xiàng zhēng zhī yī.
examples.english: The panda is one of China's symbols.

examples.chinese: 这个礼物象征着我们之间的友谊。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge lǐ wù xiàng zhēng zhe wǒ men zhī jiān de yǒu yì.
examples.english: This gift symbolizes the friendship between us.

usage_notes: Can be used as a noun ('和平的象征') or a verb ('象征友谊').

mnemonic: The '象(xiàng)' (elephant) piece is very important in Chinese '棋(qí)' (chess).
etymology: 象: elephant (also one of the pieces in the game). 棋: a general term for board games like chess or Go. Literally, 'elephant game'.

examples.chinese: 我爷爷每天都去公园下象棋。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yé ye měi tiān dōu qù gōng yuán xià xiàng qí.
examples.english: My grandpa goes to the park to play Chinese chess every day.

examples.chinese: 你会下象棋吗？教教我吧。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ huì xià xiàng qí ma? Jiāo jiao wǒ ba.
examples.english: Do you know how to play Chinese chess? Teach me.

usage_notes: The verb used is '下(xià)', as in '下象棋'. Distinct from '国际象棋 (guó jì xiàng qí)' which is Western chess.

mnemonic: The person who '负(fù)' (bears) the '责(zé)' (responsibility).
etymology: 负: to carry, to bear (a burden). 责: responsibility, duty. 人: person. Together, 'person who bears responsibility'.

examples.chinese: 这件事要找项目的负责人。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì yào zhǎo xiàng mù de fù zé rén.
examples.english: For this matter, you need to find the person in charge of the project.

examples.chinese: 他是我们部门的负责人。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì wǒ men bù mén de fù zé rén.
examples.english: He is the person in charge of our department.

usage_notes: A common and useful term in workplaces and organizations. It's a title/role, not an adjective.

english: loan; to take out/grant a loan
mnemonic: You '贷(dài)' (borrow) '款(kuǎn)' (money/funds).
etymology: 贷: to lend or borrow. 款: sum of money, funds, article. Together, it refers to a sum of money that is lent or borrowed.

examples.chinese: 我们从银行贷款买房子。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ men cóng yín háng dài kuǎn mǎi fáng zi.
examples.english: We took out a loan from the bank to buy a house.

examples.chinese: 他的公司需要一大笔贷款。
examples.pinyin: Tā de gōng sī xū yào yī dà bǐ dài kuǎn.
examples.english: His company needs a large loan.

usage_notes: Can be a verb ('贷款买房') or a noun ('一笔贷款'). '房贷(fáng dài)' is specifically a mortgage loan.

mnemonic: Think of the '贸(mào)' in '外贸(wài mào)' (foreign trade) and '易(yì)' in '交易(jiāo yì)' (transaction). It's trade!
etymology: 贸: to trade, to exchange. 易: to exchange, easy. Together, it emphasizes the exchange of goods.

examples.chinese: 中国和美国之间的贸易很重要。
examples.pinyin: Zhōng guó hé Měi guó zhī jiān de mào yì hěn zhòng yào.
examples.english: Trade between China and the US is very important.

examples.chinese: 他在一家贸易公司工作。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài yī jiā mào yì gōng sī gōng zuò.
examples.english: He works at a trading company.

usage_notes: A formal word for trade/commerce. Often used in contexts like '国际贸易', '贸易公司'.

mnemonic: A '卡(kǎ)' (card) you give to '贺(hè)' (congratulate) someone.
etymology: 贺: to congratulate, to celebrate. 卡: card (phonetic loan from English).

examples.chinese: 我每年都给朋友寄生日贺卡。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ měi nián dōu gěi péng you jì shēng rì hè kǎ.
examples.english: I send birthday cards to my friends every year.

examples.pinyin: Zhè zhāng shèng dàn hè kǎ zhēn piào liang!
examples.english: This Christmas card is really beautiful!

usage_notes: Common for birthdays, holidays, and other celebrations.

mnemonic: The '资(zī)' (capital/resources) you '产(chǎn)' (produce/own). What you own that has value.
etymology: 资: resources, capital, endowment. 产: to produce, property. Combined, it refers to property or resources owned that have economic value.

examples.chinese: 他的主要资产是房子和股票。
examples.pinyin: Tā de zhǔ yào zī chǎn shì fáng zi hé gǔ piào.
examples.english: His main assets are his house and stocks.

examples.chinese: 这家公司的资产超过十亿。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōng sī de zī chǎn chāo guò shí yì.
examples.english: This company's assets exceed one billion.

usage_notes: A formal/business/finance term for things of value owned by a person or company.

english: to sponsor; to fund; financial aid
mnemonic: To give '资(zī)' (funds) to '助(zhù)' (help/assist) someone.
etymology: 资: funds, resources. 助: to help, to assist. Together, it means to provide financial help.

examples.chinese: 他的大学学费是由一家公司资助的。
examples.pinyin: Tā de dà xué xué fèi shì yóu yī jiā gōng sī zī zhù de.
examples.english: His university tuition was sponsored by a company.

examples.chinese: 这个研究项目需要更多资助。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge yán jiū xiàng mù xū yào gèng duō zī zhù.
examples.english: This research project needs more funding.

usage_notes: Often used in formal or official contexts, like scholarships, research grants, or corporate sponsorship.

mnemonic: The '资(zī)' (funds) that is the '本(běn)' (root/base) of a business. Seed money.
etymology: 资: funds, resources. 本: root, origin, basis. Combined, it refers to the original funds used to start or run a business.

examples.chinese: 他没有足够的资本开一家新公司。
examples.pinyin: Tā méi yǒu zú gòu de zī běn kāi yī jiā xīn gōng sī.
examples.english: He doesn't have enough capital to start a new company.

examples.chinese: 在商业世界，人脉也是一种资本。
examples.pinyin: Zài shāng yè shì jiè, rén mài yě shì yī zhǒng zī běn.
examples.english: In the business world, connections are also a form of capital.

usage_notes: Mostly an economic/financial term. Can also be used metaphorically (e.g., '文化资本').

mnemonic: The '贝(bèi)' (shell/money) radical on the left gives it away — it's about money. You '赔(péi)' money when you break something.
etymology: From 貝 (shell, ancient currency) + 咅 (sound component). Originally meant to compensate for a loss.

examples.chinese: 对不起，我打破你的杯子了，我赔你一个新的。
examples.pinyin: Duì bu qǐ, wǒ dǎ pò nǐ de bēi zi le, wǒ péi nǐ yī gè xīn de.
examples.english: Sorry, I broke your cup, I'll compensate you with a new one.

examples.chinese: 这次做生意我赔了很多钱。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì zuò shēng yì wǒ péi le hěn duō qián.
examples.english: I lost a lot of money on this business deal.

usage_notes: The basic verb for compensating someone for a loss or for losing money in business. Can be used with '钱', '礼' (apologize), etc.

mnemonic: It's the formal version of '赔(péi)'. You '赔(péi)' and you '偿(cháng)' (repay).
etymology: 赔: to compensate. 偿: to repay, to fulfill. Together, it emphasizes the act of making reparations.

examples.chinese: 保险公司会赔偿你的车损。
examples.pinyin: Bǎo xiǎn gōng sī huì péi cháng nǐ de chē sǔn.
examples.english: The insurance company will compensate you for the car damage.

examples.chinese: 他们要求一百万的赔偿。
examples.pinyin: Tā men yāo qiú yī bǎi wàn de péi cháng.
examples.english: They are demanding one million in compensation.

usage_notes: More formal and legal-sounding than '赔'. Often used in contexts involving insurance, lawsuits, or formal agreements.

english: to give (as a gift); to bestow
mnemonic: The '贝(bèi)' (money) radical is involved again, but this time you're giving money/goods away for free!
etymology: From 貝 (shell/money) + 曾 (sound component). The radical suggests giving something of value.

examples.chinese: 这本书是老师赠给我的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè běn shū shì lǎo shī zèng gěi wǒ de.
examples.english: This book was given to me as a gift by my teacher.

examples.pinyin: Mǎi yī zèng yī!
examples.english: Buy one, get one free!

usage_notes: A formal/literary verb for giving a gift. Often used in fixed phrases like '买一赠一' or '赠品(zèng pǐn)' (free gift).

english: to give as a gift; to present
mnemonic: To '赠(zèng)' (give) and '送(sòng)' (send/deliver) a gift.
etymology: 赠: to give as a gift. 送: to deliver, to send, to see off. Together, it emphasizes the act of giving something away.

examples.chinese: 这个纪念品是免费赠送的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge jì niàn pǐn shì miǎn fèi zèng sòng de.
examples.english: This souvenir is given for free.

examples.chinese: 我打算把这幅画赠送给我最好的朋友。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ dǎ suàn bǎ zhè fú huà zèng sòng gěi wǒ zuì hǎo de péng you.
examples.english: I plan to give this painting as a gift to my best friend.

usage_notes: A common verb for giving gifts, often in formal or promotional contexts ('免费赠送').

english: to play a role; to serve as
mnemonic: Think of something that '起(qǐ)' (rises up/initiates) and finally '到(dào)' (reaches/achieves) an effect or role.
etymology: 起: to rise, to start. 到: to arrive, to reach. A verb complement structure indicating that an action leads to a result or effect.

examples.chinese: 你的建议起到了很大的作用。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ de jiàn yì qǐ dào le hěn dà de zuò yòng.
examples.english: Your suggestion played a very important role.

examples.chinese: 这个政策起到了积极的效果。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge zhèng cè qǐ dào le jī jí de xiào guǒ.
examples.english: This policy has had a positive effect.

usage_notes: Almost always followed by an object like '作用', '效果', '帮助'. It describes the function or effect something has.

mnemonic: The '起(qǐ)' (starting) point and '码(mǎ)' (yard/measure). The starting measure, the baseline.
etymology: 起: to start, to rise. 码: a yard, a measure, a number. Used together from Cantonese, meaning the lowest limit or starting point.

examples.chinese: 从我家到公司，起码要一个小时。
examples.pinyin: Cóng wǒ jiā dào gōng sī, qǐ mǎ yào yī gè xiǎo shí.
examples.english: It takes at least an hour to get from my home to the office.

examples.chinese: 你起码应该对他说声谢谢。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ qǐ mǎ yīng gāi duì tā shuō shēng xiè xie.
examples.english: You should at least say thank you to him.

usage_notes: Used to emphasize a minimum requirement or baseline. Slightly more colloquial than '至少'.

mnemonic: To '超(chāo)' (exceed/surpass) and '越(yuè)' (cross over/go beyond) a limit.
etymology: 超: to exceed, to overtake. 越: to cross over, to exceed. A compound with synonymous characters emphasizing exceeding limits.

examples.chinese: 他的成绩超越了班上所有人。
examples.pinyin: Tā de chéng jì chāo yuè le bān shàng suǒ yǒu rén.
examples.english: His grades surpassed everyone else's in the class.

examples.chinese: 我们的目标是超越自我。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ men de mù biāo shì chāo yuè zì wǒ.
examples.english: Our goal is to surpass ourselves.

usage_notes: Often used for surpassing others or one's own limits. Has a positive, striving connotation.

mnemonic: Right at the '跟(gēn)' (heel) and '前(qián)' (front) of someone — super close.
etymology: 跟: heel, to follow. 前: front, forward. Together, it describes a space immediately in front of someone.

examples.pinyin: Xiǎo gǒu yī zhí dāi zài wǒ gēn qián.
examples.english: The puppy keeps staying right in front of me.

examples.chinese: 他走到妈妈跟前，小声说了句话。
examples.pinyin: Tā zǒu dào mā ma gēn qián, xiǎo shēng shuō le jù huà.
examples.english: He walked up to his mom and said something quietly.

usage_notes: Specifically refers to a position very close to a person (or sometimes an object), often implying proximity for interaction.

english: to follow; to go along with
mnemonic: Think of '跟(gēn)' (to follow) and '随(suí)' (to follow/accord with). Double the following!
etymology: 跟: heel, to follow. 随: to follow, to comply with. A compound with similar meanings emphasizing close adherence.

examples.chinese: 游客们跟随着导游参观博物馆。
examples.pinyin: Yóu kè men gēn suí zhe dǎo yóu cān guān bó wù guǎn.
examples.english: The tourists followed the guide to visit the museum.

examples.chinese: 我决定跟随自己的内心。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jué dìng gēn suí zì jǐ de nèi xīn.
examples.english: I decided to follow my heart.

usage_notes: Can be used literally (following a person) or figuratively (following a trend, one's heart). Slightly more formal than '跟着'.

english: to form a set / complete with accessories
mnemonic: Think of a puzzle set; you need all the PIECES to be COMPLETE.
etymology: 配 (pèi) means 'to match' or 'distribute', 套 (tào) means 'set' or 'case'. Together it literally means 'matching set'.

examples.chinese: 这个软件和硬件是配套的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge ruǎnjiàn hé yìngjiàn shì pèitào de.
examples.english: This software and hardware are a matching set.

examples.chinese: 买了新房子，还得配套一些家具。
examples.pinyin: Mǎi le xīn fángzi, hái děi pèitào yīxiē jiājù.
examples.english: After buying a new house, we still need to get a matching set of furniture.

usage_notes: Often used as '配套设施' (pèitào shèshī) for 'supporting facilities'.

mnemonic: A GHOST (鬼) who loves WINE (酒) too much.
etymology: 酒 (jiǔ) means 'alcohol' or 'wine', 鬼 (guǐ) means 'ghost' or 'devil', implying a person possessed by drink.

examples.chinese: 他叔叔是个有名的酒鬼。
examples.pinyin: Tā shūshu shì gè yǒumíng de jiǔguǐ.
examples.english: His uncle is a famous drunkard.

examples.chinese: 别喝那么多，小心变成酒鬼。
examples.pinyin: Bié hē nàme duō, xiǎoxīn biàn chéng jiǔguǐ.
examples.english: Don't drink that much, be careful not to become an alcoholic.

usage_notes: Somewhat informal and slightly derogatory. Use with caution.

english: the joys and sorrows of life (lit. sour, sweet, bitter, spicy)
mnemonic: Imagine tasting LEMON (sour), CANDY (sweet), BEER (bitter), and CHILI (spicy) — that's LIFE.
etymology: Combines four taste sensations: 酸 (suān, sour), 甜 (tián, sweet), 苦 (kǔ, bitter), and 辣 (là, spicy). Used metaphorically.

examples.chinese: 人生中的酸甜苦辣，他都尝遍了。
examples.pinyin: Rénshēng zhōng de suāntiánkǔlà, tā dōu cháng biàn le.
examples.english: He has tasted all the joys and sorrows of life.

examples.chinese: 这道菜充满了酸甜苦辣的味道。
examples.pinyin: Zhè dào cài chōngmǎn le suāntiánkǔlà de wèidào.
examples.english: This dish is full of sour, sweet, bitter, and spicy flavors.

usage_notes: Most commonly used figuratively to describe life experiences.

mnemonic: A person leaning over (like the 酉 radical, a wine vessel) after 'celebrating' too much.
etymology: The character 醉 consists of 酉 (yǒu, originally a wine vessel) and 卒 (zú, soldier/end). Possibly implying 'ending up at the wine jar'.

examples.pinyin: Tā zuówǎn hē zuì le.
examples.english: He got drunk last night.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuìxīn yú yīnyuè.
examples.english: I am deeply fascinated by music. (lit. 'drunk-hearted')

usage_notes: Can be literal (intoxicated) or figurative (enraptured, as in 陶醉).

mnemonic: Think of a company BUYER going around with a cart (采) to PURCHASE (购) supplies.
etymology: 采 (cǎi) means 'pick' or 'gather', 购 (gòu) means 'purchase'. Together it means 'gather through purchasing'.

examples.chinese: 我负责为公司采购办公用品。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ fùzé wèi gōngsī cǎigòu bàngōng yòngpǐn.
examples.english: I am responsible for purchasing office supplies for the company.

examples.chinese: 周末要去超市进行一次大采购。
examples.pinyin: Zhōumò yào qù chāoshì jìnxíng yī cì dà cǎigòu.
examples.english: I'm going to the supermarket for a big shopping trip this weekend.

usage_notes: Often implies a planned or bulk purchase, more formal than just 买.

english: to fish (with a rod) / to angle
mnemonic: The 钅(metal) hook hanging from a line, waiting to catch a fish.
etymology: Composed of 钅(metal radical) and 勺 (sháo, spoon/ladle), originally depicting a metal hook.

examples.chinese: 周末我们去湖边钓鱼吧。
examples.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒmen qù hú biān diào yú ba.
examples.english: Let's go fishing by the lake this weekend.

examples.chinese: 他用假消息钓出了真相。
examples.pinyin: Tā yòng jiǎ xiāoxi diào chū le zhēnxiàng.
examples.english: He used false information to fish out the truth.

usage_notes: Also used metaphorically to mean 'to lure' or 'to fish for (information)'.

mnemonic: A STEEL (钢) instrument with lots of KEYS (琴).
etymology: 钢 (gāng) means 'steel', 琴 (qín) is a general term for stringed/musical instruments. A 'steel-string instrument'.

examples.chinese: 她从小就开始学弹钢琴。
examples.pinyin: Tā cóngxiǎo jiù kāishǐ xué tán gāngqín.
examples.english: She started learning to play the piano from a young age.

examples.chinese: 客厅里摆着一架黑色的钢琴。
examples.pinyin: Kètīng lǐ bǎi zhe yī jià hēisè de gāngqín.
examples.english: A black piano is placed in the living room.

usage_notes: The general measure word is 架 (jià).

mnemonic: A STEEL (钢) tip for WRITING (笔).
etymology: 钢 (gāng) means 'steel', 笔 (bǐ) means 'pen' or 'writing brush'. A 'steel(-nib) pen'.

examples.chinese: 这支钢笔是我爷爷留下的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhī gāngbǐ shì wǒ yéyé liú xià de.
examples.english: This fountain pen was left by my grandfather.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuān yòng gāngbǐ liànzì.
examples.english: I like practicing handwriting with a fountain pen.

usage_notes: Specifically refers to pens with a nib and internal ink reservoir.

mnemonic: The combination of HARD IRON (铁) and even stronger STEEL (钢).
etymology: 钢 (gāng) means 'steel', 铁 (tiě) means 'iron'. Together they represent ferrous metals.

examples.chinese: 这座桥是用钢铁建造的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò qiáo shì yòng gāngtiě jiànzào de.
examples.english: This bridge is built with steel and iron.

examples.pinyin: Tā yǒu gāngtiě bān de yìzhì.
examples.english: He has an iron will.

usage_notes: Often used metaphorically to describe something extremely strong or resilient.

mnemonic: A metal (钅) object that makes a sound (令 = command) when you ring it.
etymology: Composed of 钅(metal radical) and 令 (lìng, command). Possibly because bells were used to issue commands.

examples.chinese: 自行车上有个铃，提醒别人注意。
examples.pinyin: Zìxíngchē shàng yǒu gè líng, tǐxǐng biérén zhùyì.
examples.english: There's a bell on the bicycle to alert others.

examples.pinyin: Yáo yī yáo nàgè língdang.
examples.english: Shake that little bell.

usage_notes: Often part of compounds like 门铃 (doorbell), 铃铛 (small bell).

mnemonic: The SOUND (声) of a BELL (铃).
etymology: 铃 (líng) 'bell' + 声 (shēng) 'sound' = 'sound of a bell'.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ de shǒujī língshēng tài chǎo le.
examples.english: Your phone ringtone is too loud.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ tīng dào le shàngkè de língshēng.
examples.english: I heard the class bell ringing.

usage_notes: In modern context, almost always refers to a phone ringtone.

mnemonic: A metal (钅) device that makes something SMALL (肖) and inaccessible.
etymology: Composed of 钅(metal) and 肖 (xiào, resembling/small). The exact connection is debated, possibly depicting a small metal fastener.

examples.pinyin: Chūmén qián bié wàng le suǒ mén.
examples.english: Don't forget to lock the door before going out.

examples.pinyin: Zhè bǎ suǒ huài le, dǎ bù kāi.
examples.english: This lock is broken and won't open.

usage_notes: Common verb-noun. Also used in computing (锁定 suǒdìng - to lock).

mnemonic: A metal (钅) container for cooking, looks like a pot with a lid (呙).
etymology: Simplified from 鍋, composed of 钅(metal) and 呙 (wāi, crooked/region), possibly indicating a curved vessel.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ yòng zhè kǒu guō chǎocài.
examples.english: I use this wok to stir-fry.

examples.pinyin: Zhè ge guō de guōdǐ shāo hú le.
examples.english: The bottom of this pot is burnt.

usage_notes: Common measure word is 口 (kǒu). 背锅 (bēi guō) means 'to take the blame'.

mnemonic: A metal (钅) thing you BUILD (建) a sequence with, like keys on a keyboard.
etymology: Composed of 钅(metal) and 建 (jiàn, to build). Likely because keys are metal components you 'build' an interface with.

examples.pinyin: Jiànpán shàng de 'A' jiàn zài nǎlǐ?
examples.english: Where is the 'A' key on the keyboard?

examples.pinyin: Àn zhège jiàn jiù kěyǐ jiétú.
examples.english: Press this key to take a screenshot.

usage_notes: Most often refers to keys on a keyboard or buttons on a device.

mnemonic: A BOARD (盘) full of KEYS (键).
etymology: 键 (jiàn) 'key' + 盘 (pán) 'tray/board' = 'keyboard'.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ de jiànpán yǒudiǎn zāng le.
examples.english: My keyboard is a bit dirty.

examples.chinese: 他买了一个机械键盘打游戏。
examples.pinyin: Tā mǎi le yī gè jīxiè jiànpán dǎ yóuxì.
examples.english: He bought a mechanical keyboard for gaming.

usage_notes: Refers to computer, piano, or any instrument keyboard.

mnemonic: Having a LONG (长) LIFE (寿).
etymology: 长 (cháng) 'long' + 寿 (shòu) 'longevity'.

examples.pinyin: Zhù nín jiànkāng chángshòu!
examples.english: Wishing you health and longevity!

examples.pinyin: Zhège dìqū de rén hěn chángshòu.
examples.english: People in this region live very long lives.

usage_notes: A very common and positive blessing, especially for the elderly.

mnemonic: The DEGREE (度) of how LONG (长) something is.
etymology: 长 (cháng) 'long' + 度 (dù) 'degree/measure' = 'measure of length'.

examples.chinese: 这条裙子的长度正合适。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo qúnzi de chángdù zhèng héshì.
examples.english: The length of this skirt is just right.

examples.chinese: 你知道这条河的长度吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zhīdào zhè tiáo hé de chángdù ma?
examples.english: Do you know the length of this river?

usage_notes: A standard measurement term.

mnemonic: The DOOR (门) where they DIAGNOSE (诊) you (without staying overnight).
etymology: 门 (mén) 'door/gate' + 诊 (zhěn) 'diagnose' = 'place for diagnosis you walk into', i.e., outpatient clinic.

examples.chinese: 我挂了一个明天早上的门诊号。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ guà le yī gè míngtiān zǎoshang de ménzhěn hào.
examples.english: I booked an outpatient appointment for tomorrow morning.

examples.pinyin: Érkē ménzhěn zài èr lóu.
examples.english: The pediatric outpatient clinic is on the second floor.

usage_notes: Contrasts with 住院 (zhùyuàn, hospitalization).

english: to close (a meeting, festival, etc.) / to conclude
mnemonic: CLOSE (闭) the CURTAIN (幕) on an event.
etymology: 闭 (bì) 'to close' + 幕 (mù) 'curtain' = 'to close the curtain'.

examples.chinese: 运动会将于明天下午闭幕。
examples.pinyin: Yùndònghuì jiāng yú míngtiān xiàwǔ bìmù.
examples.english: The sports meet will close tomorrow afternoon.

examples.chinese: 他的演讲为活动拉开了闭幕。
examples.pinyin: Tā de yǎnjiǎng wèi huódòng lākāi le bìmù.
examples.english: His speech drew the event to a close.

usage_notes: Opposite of 开幕 (kāimù). Usually for formal events.

mnemonic: The formal CEREMONY (式) of CLOSING (闭幕).
etymology: 闭幕 (bìmù) 'to close' + 式 (shì) 'ceremony/form' = 'closing ceremony'.

examples.chinese: 奥运会的闭幕式非常精彩。
examples.pinyin: Àoyùnhuì de bìmùshì fēicháng jīngcǎi.
examples.english: The Olympic closing ceremony was spectacular.

examples.chinese: 谁主持了今晚的闭幕式？
examples.pinyin: Shéi zhǔchí le jīn wǎn de bìmùshì?
examples.english: Who hosted tonight's closing ceremony?

usage_notes: The formal counterpart to 开幕式 (kāimùshì).

english: to rush / to charge / to barge in
mnemonic: A HORSE (马) rushing through a DOOR (门).
etymology: Composed of 门 (mén, gate/door) and 马 (mǎ, horse), depicting a horse charging through a gate.

examples.chinese: 他直接闯进了我的办公室。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhíjiē chuǎng jìn le wǒ de bàngōngshì.
examples.english: He barged right into my office.

examples.pinyin: Bùyào chuǎng hóngdēng, tài wēixiǎn le!
examples.english: Don't run the red light, it's too dangerous!

usage_notes: Often implies a sense of force, rudeness, or rule-breaking (e.g., 闯红灯).

mnemonic: A DOOR (门) with a TREE (木) behind it — a peaceful, idle scene.
etymology: Traditional 閑/閒: 門 (door/gate) + 木 (tree) — perhaps depicting leisure behind a closed gate.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ jīntiān xiàwǔ hěn xián.
examples.english: I'm free this afternoon.

examples.pinyin: Bié guǎn xiánshì.
examples.english: Don't meddle in other people's business (lit. 'idle matters').

usage_notes: Opposite of 忙 (máng). 闲事 means 'other people's business'.

mnemonic: Through an INTERVAL (间) before making a CONNECTION (接) — not direct.
etymology: 间 (jiān/jiàn) 'interval/separate' + 接 (jiē) 'connect' = 'connected through an interval'.

examples.chinese: 我是间接知道这个消息的。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ shì jiànjiē zhīdào zhège xiāoxi de.
examples.english: I learned this news indirectly.

examples.chinese: 吸烟也会对家人造成间接伤害。
examples.pinyin: Xīyān yě huì duì jiārén zàochéng jiànjiē shānghài.
examples.english: Smoking can also cause indirect harm to family members.

usage_notes: Opposite of 直接 (zhíjiē). Often used in formal or logical contexts.

mnemonic: A ROOM (室) for READING (阅览).
etymology: 阅览 (yuèlǎn) 'to read and look over' + 室 (shì) 'room'.

examples.chinese: 图书馆的阅览室里很安静。
examples.pinyin: Túshūguǎn de yuèlǎnshì lǐ hěn ānjìng.
examples.english: It's very quiet in the library's reading room.

examples.chinese: 我通常在阅览室做作业。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ tōngcháng zài yuèlǎnshì zuò zuòyè.
examples.english: I usually do my homework in the reading room.

usage_notes: Common in schools, libraries, and some offices.

mnemonic: First GUARD AGAINST (防) it, then MANAGE (治) it if it happens.
etymology: 防 (fáng) 'prevent/guard against' + 治 (zhì) 'control/treat'.

examples.chinese: 我们要做好病虫害的防治工作。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào zuò hǎo bìngchónghài de fángzhì gōngzuò.
examples.english: We need to do a good job in pest and disease prevention and control.

examples.chinese: 这种病的防治方法很重要。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng bìng de fángzhì fāngfǎ hěn zhòngyào.
examples.english: The prevention and control methods for this disease are very important.

usage_notes: Commonly used in public health, agriculture, and environmental contexts.

mnemonic: Think of 'duǒ' as 'dodge' – you need to dodge or hide from something.
etymology: From ⾝ (body) + 朵 (a phonetic component suggesting shape/sound). The original meaning relates to the body taking cover.

examples.chinese: 快下雨了，我们找个地方躲一下吧。
examples.pinyin: Kuài xià yǔ le, wǒ men zhǎo gè dì fang duǒ yī xià ba.
examples.english: It's about to rain, let's find a place to take shelter.

examples.pinyin: Tā zǒng duǒ zhe wǒ, bù xiǎng huán qián.
examples.english: He always avoids me because he doesn't want to pay back the money.

usage_notes: Often used with 在, 到, or 过。 '躲起来' means to hide oneself away.

mnemonic: '转' (turn/change) + '化' (change into). It's about changing one thing *into* another.
etymology: Compound word: 转 (to turn, change) + 化 (to change into, -ize).

examples.chinese: 太阳能可以转化为电能。
examples.pinyin: Tài yáng néng kě yǐ zhuǎn huà wéi diàn néng.
examples.english: Solar energy can be converted into electrical energy.

examples.chinese: 他把压力转化成了动力。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ yā lì zhuǎn huà chéng le dòng lì.
examples.english: He transformed pressure into motivation.

usage_notes: Often used with 为, 成, or 到 to indicate the result of the transformation.

mnemonic: '转' (turn) + '向' (toward/direction). You turn toward a new direction.
etymology: Compound word: 转 (to turn) + 向 (direction, towards).

examples.pinyin: Qián miàn lù kǒu xiàng zuǒ zhuǎn xiàng.
examples.english: Turn left at the intersection ahead.

examples.chinese: 他的职业方向完全转向了。
examples.pinyin: Tā de zhí yè fāng xiàng wán quán zhuǎn xiàng le.
examples.english: His career direction has completely shifted.

usage_notes: Can be literal (driving) or figurative (changing a course of action). Distinguish from 转弯 which is specifically 'make a turn'.

mnemonic: '转' (turn) + '换' (exchange). You turn and exchange one thing for another.
etymology: Compound word: 转 (to turn, change) + 换 (to exchange).

examples.chinese: 把电视转换到游戏模式。
examples.pinyin: Bǎ diàn shì zhuǎn huàn dào yóu xì mó shì.
examples.english: Switch the TV to game mode.

examples.chinese: 我们需要转换一下心情。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ men xū yào zhuǎn huàn yī xià xīn qíng.
examples.english: We need to change our mood (switch gears).

usage_notes: Often used for switching between modes, channels, states of mind, or systems.

mnemonic: '转' (transfer) + '让' (to let). You transfer and let someone else have it.
etymology: Compound word: 转 (to transfer) + 让 (to yield, to let).

examples.chinese: 我想转让这家店的会员卡。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng zhuǎn ràng zhè jiā diàn de huì yuán kǎ.
examples.english: I want to transfer the membership card for this shop.

examples.chinese: 他决定把公司转让给朋友。
examples.pinyin: Tā jué dìng bǎ gōng sī zhuǎn ràng gěi péng you.
examples.english: He decided to transfer the company to a friend.

usage_notes: Used for formal transfers of rights, tickets, leases, businesses, etc.

mnemonic: Think of 'ruǎn' sounding like 'ruin' – something soft can be easily ruined? Or picture a soft cushion.
etymology: From ⾞ (cart) + 欠 (to owe). The original meaning is debated, but the modern meaning is 'soft, pliable'.

examples.chinese: 这个沙发太软了，坐得很舒服。
examples.pinyin: Zhè gè shā fā tài ruǎn le, zuò de hěn shū fu.
examples.english: This sofa is too soft, it's very comfortable to sit on.

examples.pinyin: Tā shì gè xīn hěn ruǎn de rén.
examples.english: He is a soft-hearted person.

usage_notes: Opposite of 硬 (hard). Can describe texture, personality (soft-hearted), or market conditions (soft market).

english: to look down on, to despise
mnemonic: '轻' (light/unimportant) + '视' (to look at). You look at someone/thing as if they are light/insignificant.
etymology: Compound word: 轻 (light, trivial) + 视 (to look at, regard).

examples.chinese: 不要轻视任何人的努力。
examples.pinyin: Bù yào qīng shì rèn hé rén de nǔ lì.
examples.english: Don't look down on anyone's efforts.

examples.pinyin: Tā yīn wèi xué lì bèi qīng shì le.
examples.english: He was looked down upon because of his educational background.

usage_notes: Similar to 看不起, but can sound slightly more formal or literary.

mnemonic: '辅' (to assist) + '助' (to help). Double helping!
etymology: Compound word: 辅 (to assist, side of a cart) + 助 (to help).

examples.chinese: 这个工具是辅助学习的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè gè gōng jù shì fǔ zhù xué xí de.
examples.english: This tool is for assisting learning.

examples.chinese: 他在团队里做辅助工作。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài tuán duì lǐ zuò fǔ zhù gōng zuò.
examples.english: He does auxiliary work in the team.

usage_notes: As an adjective, it describes something supplementary or secondary (e.g., 辅助设备 - auxiliary equipment).

mnemonic: Think of the radical ⾮ (non-), suggesting 'not the same' – people of different generations are not the same. Also used in 一辈子 (one lifetime).
etymology: From ⾮ (not, oppose) + ⾞ (cart). The original meaning related to a hundred carts, later used metaphorically for ranks or generations.

examples.pinyin: Tā shì wǒ de zhǎng bèi.
examples.english: He is my elder/senior.

examples.chinese: 我这辈子都没见过这种事。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhè bèi zi dōu méi jiàn guò zhè zhǒng shì.
examples.english: I've never seen such a thing in my whole life.

usage_notes: Most commonly used in compounds like 长辈, 晚辈, or as a measure word for generations (几辈人). The word 一辈子 is a very common phrase.

mnemonic: '输' (transport/lose) + '出' (out). Sending something out. (Think: your computer 'loses' data out to the screen/printer).
etymology: Compound word: 输 (to transport, to lose) + 出 (to go out).

examples.pinyin: Bǎ jié guǒ shū chū dào wén jiàn lǐ.
examples.english: Output the results to a file.

examples.chinese: 这个国家主要输出石油。
examples.pinyin: Zhè gè guó jiā zhǔ yào shū chū shí yóu.
examples.english: This country mainly exports oil.

usage_notes: The opposite is 输入 (input/import). Used in technology (data output) and economics (exports).

english: hard, strenuous; to go to trouble
mnemonic: '辛' (spicy/hardship) + '苦' (bitter). Hard work tastes spicy and bitter.
etymology: Compound word: 辛 (pungent, toil) + 苦 (bitter, hardship).

examples.pinyin: Nín xīn kǔ le!
examples.english: Thank you for your hard work! (A very common polite phrase)

examples.pinyin: Zuì jìn gōng zuò tè bié xīn kǔ.
examples.english: Work has been particularly hard lately.

usage_notes: A very high-frequency word. Can be used as an adjective or as a polite verb (辛苦你了 - Sorry to trouble you / Thanks for your effort).

mnemonic: '辞' (to decline, say goodbye to) + '职' (position/post). You say goodbye to your post.
etymology: Compound word: 辞 (to decline, take leave) + 职 (position, duty).

examples.pinyin: Tā zuó tiān xiàng lǎo bǎn cí zhí le.
examples.english: He resigned to his boss yesterday.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ dǎ suàn xià gè yuè cí zhí.
examples.english: I plan to resign next month.

usage_notes: A formal act. For casual quitting, you can also say 不干了.

mnemonic: '达' (reach/achieve) + '成' (accomplish). Double accomplishment!
etymology: Compound word: 达 (to reach, attain) + 成 (to accomplish, succeed).

examples.pinyin: Shuāng fāng zhōng yú dá chéng le yī zhì.
examples.english: The two sides finally reached an agreement.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ men dá chéng le hé zuò yì xiàng.
examples.english: We have reached an intent to cooperate.

usage_notes: Almost always used for abstract things like agreements, consensus, intentions, etc.

mnemonic: '过' (exceed) + '于' (a classical preposition). It exceeds the normal limit.
etymology: From the classical structure 过 (to exceed) + 于 (at, in).

examples.pinyin: Nǐ guò yú dān xīn le, méi shì de.
examples.english: You're worrying too much, it's fine.

examples.chinese: 这衣服的颜色过于鲜艳。
examples.pinyin: Zhè yī fu de yán sè guò yú xiān yàn.
examples.english: The color of this clothing is too bright.

usage_notes: Used before adjectives or some verbs. Slightly more formal than 太, but still common in spoken language for emphasis.

mnemonic: '过' (exceed) + '度' (degree/limit). It exceeds the proper degree.
etymology: Compound word: 过 (to exceed) + 度 (degree, limit).

examples.pinyin: Guò dù yǐn jiǔ duì shēn tǐ bù hǎo.
examples.english: Excessive drinking is bad for your health.

examples.chinese: 他因为过度疲劳住院了。
examples.pinyin: Tā yīn wèi guò dù pí láo zhù yuàn le.
examples.english: He was hospitalized due to overwork/excessive fatigue.

usage_notes: Used as an adjective (过度的工作) or adverb (过度使用). Often implies a negative consequence.

mnemonic: One character, two main uses: moving goods (🚚) and moving fortune (🍀).
etymology: Simplified from 運. From ⾰ (walk) + 軍 (army), suggesting movement of troops, hence to transport. The 'luck' meaning is an extension.

examples.pinyin: Zhè pī huò yào yùn dào Shàng hǎi.
examples.english: This batch of goods needs to be transported to Shanghai.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ jīn tiān yùn qì zhēn hǎo!
examples.english: I have such good luck today!

usage_notes: As a single character, it's often part of compounds. 运 by itself as a verb is common (运货). For 'luck', it's almost always 运气.

mnemonic: '运' (move/operate) + '行' (go/perform). Something (like a machine) is moving and performing its function.
etymology: Compound word: 运 (to move, operate) + 行 (to go, to do).

examples.pinyin: Zhè gè chéng xù yùn xíng de hěn màn.
examples.english: This program runs very slowly.

examples.chinese: 地铁晚上十点停止运行。
examples.pinyin: Dì tiě wǎn shàng shí diǎn tíng zhǐ yùn xíng.
examples.english: The subway stops operating at 10 PM.

usage_notes: Used for machines, vehicles, software, systems, plans, etc.

mnemonic: '近' (near) + '来' (come). The time that has come near to now.
etymology: Compound word: 近 (near) + 来 (to come).

examples.pinyin: Nǐ jìn lái zěn me yàng?
examples.english: How have you been lately?

examples.pinyin: Jìn lái tiān qì biàn huà hěn dà.
examples.english: The weather has been changing a lot recently.

usage_notes: Very similar to 最近. Can be used at the beginning of a sentence or after the subject.

mnemonic: '返' (return) + '回' (return). Double return! (返 and 回 are synonyms).
etymology: Compound word: 返 (to return) + 回 (to return).

examples.chinese: 我们什么时候返回学校？
examples.pinyin: Wǒ men shén me shí hou fǎn huí xué xiào?
examples.english: When are we returning to school?

examples.chinese: 按这个键可以返回主菜单。
examples.pinyin: Àn zhè gè jiàn kě yǐ fǎn huí zhǔ cài dān.
examples.english: Press this key to return to the main menu.

usage_notes: Slightly more formal or technical than just 回 or 回来. Common in tech (return to a page) and formal travel contexts.

mnemonic: Imagine a road blocked by a big stone (阻) that prevents (碍) you from passing.
etymology: 阻 (zǔ) means 'to obstruct, block'. 碍 (ài) means 'to hinder, obstruct'. Combined, it strongly emphasizes the act of blocking.

examples.chinese: 路上的事故严重阻碍了交通。
examples.pinyin: Lù shàng de shìgù yánzhòng zǔ'àile jiāotōng.
examples.english: The accident on the road severely hindered traffic.

examples.chinese: 不要让你的恐惧阻碍你前进。
examples.pinyin: Bùyào ràng nǐ de kǒngjù zǔ'ài nǐ qiánjìn.
examples.english: Don't let your fear stop you from moving forward.

usage_notes: Can be used both as a verb (阻碍发展) and a noun (遇到了阻碍).

mnemonic: Think of it as the additional (附) item (件) you add to an email.
etymology: 附 (fù) means 'to attach, add'. 件 (jiàn) is a measure word for items/things. Together, it means an attached item.

examples.chinese: 我把照片放在邮件的附件里了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bǎ zhàopiàn fàng zài yóujiàn de fùjiàn lǐ le.
examples.english: I put the photo in the email attachment.

examples.chinese: 这个手机的附件包括充电器和耳机。
examples.pinyin: Zhège shǒujī de fùjiàn bāokuò chōngdiàn qì hé ěrjī.
examples.english: The accessories for this phone include a charger and earphones.

usage_notes: Very common in digital contexts (email, file attachments). Also used for physical accessories.

mnemonic: It's the night that 'removes' (除) the old year and welcomes the 'evening' (夕) of the new.
etymology: 除 (chú) originally meant 'to remove, step over'. 夕 (xī) means 'evening, sunset'. Together, it symbolizes 'removing the old year on its last evening'.

examples.chinese: 我们全家在除夕一起吃年夜饭。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen quánjiā zài Chúxī yīqǐ chī niányèfàn.
examples.english: Our whole family eats the reunion dinner together on Chinese New Year's Eve.

examples.chinese: 除夕晚上，外面都是鞭炮声。
examples.pinyin: Chúxī wǎnshang, wàimiàn dōu shì biānpào shēng.
examples.english: On New Year's Eve, it's all firecracker sounds outside.

usage_notes: A proper noun for a specific festival day, often capitalized in pinyin. The most important family gathering in Chinese culture.

mnemonic: It's the condition that 'removes' (除) the possibility 'unless' (非) it's met.
etymology: 除 (chú) means 'to remove, except'. 非 (fēi) means 'not, unless'. Together, it sets an exclusive condition.

examples.chinese: 除非下雨，否则我们明天去公园。
examples.pinyin: Chúfēi xià yǔ, fǒuzé wǒmen míngtiān qù gōngyuán.
examples.english: Unless it rains, we'll go to the park tomorrow.

examples.chinese: 我周末不加班，除非老板要求。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhōumò bù jiābān, chúfēi lǎobǎn yāoqiú.
examples.english: I don't work overtime on weekends, unless the boss asks.

usage_notes: Often used in a structure "除非 A，否则/才 B" (Unless A, otherwise/then B). It introduces the only exception.

english: to accompany; to keep someone company
mnemonic: Think of standing next to (⻖ radical) someone and 'matching' (咅 component) their pace.
etymology: The character combines the 'mound/place' radical (阝 on the left) with 咅 (pǒu), a phonetic component. It implies being alongside someone.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ néng péi wǒ qù guàngjiē ma?
examples.english: Can you accompany me to go shopping?

examples.chinese: 他生病的时候，我一直在医院陪他。
examples.pinyin: Tā shēngbìng de shíhou, wǒ yīzhí zài yīyuàn péi tā.
examples.english: When he was sick, I stayed at the hospital to keep him company.

usage_notes: A very common verb for doing things together with someone, showing care or companionship.

mnemonic: It means 'following' (随) 'after' (后) in time.
etymology: 随 (suí) means 'to follow, along with'. 后 (hòu) means 'after, behind'. Together, they mean 'following closely after'.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ xiān zǒu, wǒ suíhòu jiù dào.
examples.english: You go first, I'll arrive soon after.

examples.chinese: 他发了信息，随后又打了个电话。
examples.pinyin: Tā fāle xìnxī, suíhòu yòu dǎle gè diànhuà.
examples.english: He sent a message, and soon after made a phone call.

usage_notes: Indicates an action happening shortly after a previous one. Similar to 'shortly afterwards'.

mnemonic: It means 'following' (随) your own 'intentions/wishes' (意).
etymology: 随 (suí) means 'to follow'. 意 (yì) means 'intention, wish'. So it means 'following one's own wishes'.

examples.chinese: 请随意，就像在自己家一样。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng suíyì, jiù xiàng zài zìjǐ jiā yīyàng.
examples.english: Please make yourself at home, just like in your own house.

examples.chinese: 今天的着装要求很随意。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān de zhuózhuó yāoqiú hěn suíyì.
examples.english: Today's dress code is very casual.

usage_notes: Often used as a polite invitation (请随意). Slightly more refined than 随便.

mnemonic: It shows something happening 'following' (随) and 'attached to' (着) another change.
etymology: 随 (suí) means 'to follow'. 着 (zhe) is a grammatical particle indicating continuation. Together, they form a preposition.

examples.chinese: 随着技术的发展，我们的生活改变了很多。
examples.pinyin: Suízhe jìshù de fāzhǎn, wǒmen de shēnghuó gǎibiànle hěn duō.
examples.english: Along with the development of technology, our lives have changed a lot.

examples.chinese: 随着年龄增长，他越来越稳重了。
examples.pinyin: Suízhe niánlíng zēngzhǎng, tā yuè lái yuè wěnzhòng le.
examples.english: As he gets older, he's becoming more and more steady.

usage_notes: Used at the beginning of a sentence to introduce a background condition or trend that causes a change. Often paired with 的.

mnemonic: It's the house separated by a 'partition' (隔) on the 'wall' (壁).
etymology: 隔 (gé) means 'to separate, partition'. 壁 (bì) means 'wall'. So it literally means 'separated by a wall', i.e., next door.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhù zài nǐ jiā gébì.
examples.english: I live next door to you.

examples.chinese: 隔壁老王经常来借东西。
examples.pinyin: Gébì Lǎo Wáng jīngcháng lái jiè dōngxi.
examples.english: Old Wang next door often comes to borrow things.

usage_notes: Can refer to the adjacent space (隔壁房间) or the neighbor (我隔壁).

mnemonic: It describes something so 'difficult' (难) that it's 'impossible to' (以) easily do.
etymology: 难 (nán) means 'difficult'. 以 (yǐ) here is a classical particle meaning 'to, in order to'. Together, they form a fixed phrase meaning 'hard to'.

examples.chinese: 这个数学题真是难以理解。
examples.pinyin: Zhège shùxuétí zhēnshi nányǐ lǐjiě.
examples.english: This math problem is really hard to understand.

examples.chinese: 我难以忘记那天的经历。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ nányǐ wàngjì nà tiān de jīnglì.
examples.english: It's hard for me to forget that day's experience.

usage_notes: Almost always followed by a verb (难以 + V). It's more formal/written than 很难 but common in speech for emphasis.

mnemonic: Something so good it's 'hard' (难) to 'obtain' (得).
etymology: 难 (nán) means 'difficult'. 得 (dé) means 'to obtain, get'. So it describes something difficult to obtain, hence rare.

examples.chinese: 这么便宜的机票真是难得。
examples.pinyin: Zhème piányí de jīpiào zhēnshi nándé.
examples.english: Such cheap flight tickets are really rare.

examples.chinese: 难得今天大家都有空，我们聚一聚吧。
examples.pinyin: Nándé jīntiān dàjiā dōu yǒu kòng, wǒmen jù yī jù ba.
examples.english: It's rare that everyone is free today, let's get together.

usage_notes: Often used to praise an opportunity or quality. Can also be used as an adverb (难得见面).

mnemonic: Think of something 'powerful' (雄) and 'towering' (伟) like a great mountain or palace.
etymology: 雄 (xióng) means 'male, powerful, heroic'. 伟 (wěi) means 'great, mighty'. Together, they describe grandeur and imposing scale.

examples.pinyin: Gùgōng de jiànzhù fēicháng xióngwěi.
examples.english: The architecture of the Forbidden City is extremely magnificent.

examples.chinese: 我们看到了一座雄伟的大桥。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen kàndàole yī zuò xióngwěi de dàqiáo.
examples.english: We saw a grand bridge.

usage_notes: Used to describe large-scale man-made structures (buildings, bridges) or natural landscapes (mountains).

mnemonic: A 'collective' (集) 'team' (团) of companies.
etymology: 集 (jí) means 'to gather, collection'. 团 (tuán) means 'group, regiment'. Together, it refers to a large organized group.

examples.chinese: 他在一家大型互联网集团工作。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài yī jiā dàxíng hùliánwǎng jítuán gōngzuò.
examples.english: He works at a large internet conglomerate.

examples.chinese: 这个餐饮集团有很多分店。
examples.pinyin: Zhège cānyǐn jítuán yǒu hěn duō fēndiàn.
examples.english: This restaurant group has many branches.

usage_notes: Commonly used for business conglomerates (阿里巴巴集团) but can also refer to other organized groups.

mnemonic: Simply 'rain' (雨) 'water' (水).
etymology: 雨 (yǔ) means 'rain'. 水 (shuǐ) means 'water'. A straightforward compound.

examples.pinyin: Yòng tǒng jiē yīxiē yǔshuǐ jiāo huā.
examples.english: Use a bucket to collect some rainwater to water the plants.

examples.chinese: 雨水节气意味着降雨会增多。
examples.pinyin: Yǔshuǐ jiéqì yìwèizhe jiàngyǔ huì zēng duō.
examples.english: The 'Rain Water' solar term means rainfall will increase.

usage_notes: In everyday use, it means rainwater. Capitalized (Yǔshuǐ) it's the 2nd of the 24 solar terms, around Feb 18-20.

mnemonic: The character looks like rain (雨) over a field (田), where thunder strikes.
etymology: A pictogram. The top 雨 (yǔ) is 'rain', the bottom was originally a depiction of lightning. It represents thunder, associated with storms.

examples.chinese: 刚才打了一个好响的雷！
examples.pinyin: Gāngcái dǎle yī gè hǎo xiǎng de léi!
examples.english: There was a really loud clap of thunder just now!

examples.chinese: 这个电视剧的剧情太雷了。
examples.pinyin: Zhège diànshìjù de jùqíng tài léi le.
examples.english: The plot of this TV drama is so shockingly bad (lit. 'thunderous').

usage_notes: Literal meaning is thunder. In internet slang, 雷人/太雷了 means something is bizarre, shocking, or cringe-worthy.

mnemonic: It feels like an 'earthquake' (震) that 'surprises' (惊) you.
etymology: 震 (zhèn) means 'to shake, quake'. 惊 (jīng) means 'to startle, surprise'. Combined, it means 'shaken with surprise'.

examples.chinese: 听到这个消息，所有人都震惊了。
examples.pinyin: Tīngdào zhège xiāoxi, suǒyǒu rén dōu zhènjīng le.
examples.english: Upon hearing this news, everyone was shocked.

examples.chinese: 他的行为震惊了整个社区。
examples.pinyin: Tā de xíngwéi zhènjīngle zhěnggè shèqū.
examples.english: His actions shocked the whole community.

usage_notes: Describes a strong emotional reaction to unexpected and often negative news or events.

mnemonic: It's the color of lush plants (the bottom part 月 is actually 丹, a dye vessel) under the sky.
etymology: An ancient character depicting plants growing from a dye vat. It originally covered a range of colors from blue to green, symbolizing vitality.

examples.pinyin: Yuǎnchù de shān shì qīng sè de.
examples.english: The mountains in the distance are bluish-green.

examples.chinese: 他是我们公司的一个青年才俊。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì wǒmen gōngsī de yīgè qīngnián cáijùn.
examples.english: He is a talented young man in our company.

usage_notes: A complex color term. Can mean green (青菜), blue (青天), or black (青衣 in opera). Also used in 青年 (youth) and 青春 (youthfulness).

english: to approach; to be close to
mnemonic: To 'lean against' (靠) and get 'near' (近).
etymology: 靠 (kào) means 'to lean on, rely on'. 近 (jìn) means 'near, close'. Together, they mean to move physically close to something.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng wù kàojìn shīgōng xiànchǎng.
examples.english: Please do not approach the construction site.

examples.chinese: 我家靠近地铁站，很方便。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiā kàojìn dìtiě zhàn, hěn fāngbiàn.
examples.english: My home is close to the subway station, very convenient.

usage_notes: Can be used for both moving closer (verb) and describing proximity (adjective-like).

mnemonic: It's the 'face' (面) 'son' (子) you present to society to maintain respect.
etymology: 面 (miàn) means 'face'. 子 (zi) is a nominal suffix. It's a metaphor for social image and honor.

examples.chinese: 他当众批评我，让我很没面子。
examples.pinyin: Tā dāngzhòng pīpíng wǒ, ràng wǒ hěn méi miànzi.
examples.english: He criticized me in public, which made me lose a lot of face.

examples.chinese: 看在朋友的面子上，我就帮你这一次。
examples.pinyin: Kàn zài péngyou de miànzi shàng, wǒ jiù bāng nǐ zhè yī cì.
examples.english: For the sake of our friendship (lit. for my friend's face), I'll help you this time.
